terminology.decree: Judgment of Divorce Nisi / Judgment of Divorce Absolute
terminology.nisiPeriod: 90 days after Judgment of Divorce Nisi before Divorce is Absolute

residencyRequirements.description: If the cause of action arose in Massachusetts, the plaintiff need only be domiciled in Massachusetts at the time of filing. If the cause occurred outside Massachusetts, both parties must have been domiciled in Massachusetts, OR one party must have been domiciled in Massachusetts for one (1) year preceding the complaint.

waitingPeriod.description: Massachusetts has a 90-day 'nisi' period. After the court enters a Judgment of Divorce Nisi, the divorce does not become absolute until 90 days later (Judgment of Divorce Absolute). M.G.L. c. 208, § 21.

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown of Marriage (Joint Petition)
noFault.description: Both parties file a joint petition alleging irretrievable breakdown. A 6-month waiting period from the date of filing is required before the court may hold a hearing and enter judgment. The separation agreement must be filed simultaneously.

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown of Marriage (Unilateral)
noFault.description: One party files alleging irretrievable breakdown. Requires a 6-month waiting period from the date of filing before a hearing can be held.

fault.name: Utter Desertion for One Year
fault.description: Utter desertion continued for one (1) year next prior to the filing of the complaint.

fault.name: Gross and Confirmed Habits of Intoxication Caused by Voluntary Use of Intoxicating Liquor, Opium, or Other Drug
Sentence to Imprisonment for Five or More Years
Gross, Wanton, and Cruel Neglect to Provide Suitable Maintenance for Spouse

propertyDivision.description: Massachusetts divides all property equitably — including all property of each party regardless of how or when it was acquired, including pre-marital property and inherited property. The court considers the factors in M.G.L. c. 208, § 34.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Unlike many states, Massachusetts does NOT automatically exclude pre-marital property or inherited property from division. The court has broad discretion to divide all property equitably.

alimony.description: Massachusetts awards several types of alimony under M.G.L. c. 208, § 48 et seq. The 2011 Alimony Reform Act established types and durational limits. General term alimony for marriages of 5+ years has statutory durational limits based on marriage length.

filingFees.notes: Massachusetts Probate and Family Court filing fees are approximately $215 for a Complaint for Divorce. Fee waivers (Affidavit of Indigency) are available for qualifying individuals.

basic.name: Complaint for Divorce (CJ-D 101A / CJ-D 101B)
basic.description: CJ-D 101A for joint petition (§ 1A); CJ-D 101B for contested (§ 1B) or fault-based divorce

basic.name: Financial Statement (CJ-D 301S / CJ-D 301L)
basic.description: Short form (CJ-D 301S) if income under $75,000; Long form (CJ-D 301L) if income $75,000 or more

basic.name: Vital Statistics Worksheet (R-408)
basic.description: Required statistical information for the Registry of Vital Records

basic.name: Certificate of Absolute Divorce or Annulment (R-408)

service.name: Acceptance of Service
service.description: Defendant accepts service without formal process

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation under Massachusetts Child Support Guidelines

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Proposed custody and parenting time schedule
withChildren.notes: Required for joint petition (§ 1A) divorce; strongly recommended for all cases with children

withChildren.name: Affidavit Disclosing Care or Custody Proceedings (UCCJEA Affidavit)
withChildren.description: Required disclosure of any other custody proceedings

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Massachusetts Rules of Domestic Relations Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Massachusetts must file an answer within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Massachusetts uses an income shares model under the Massachusetts Child Support Guidelines. Both parents' gross incomes are considered. The guidelines provide a formula based on combined available income and the number of children. The guidelines are reviewed and updated periodically by the Trial Court.
childSupportGuidelines.statute: Massachusetts Child Support Guidelines (M.G.L. c. 208, § 28; M.G.L. c. 209C, § 9)
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The guidelines were most recently updated effective June 15, 2018. Courts may deviate from the guidelines for good cause.

court.name: Probate and Family Court Department
court.description: Divorce actions in Massachusetts are filed in the Probate and Family Court in the county where either party lives. Massachusetts has abolished county government but courts remain organized by county division.
